title: Unhuman Tour (*Kusamakura*)
author: Natsume Sōseki (tr. Kazutomo Takahashi)
note:
Before-sleep ritual sit — climbing toward Nakoi.

Climbing toward the spa, a painter decides this human world is unbearable—and that an “unhuman” one would be worse. Poetry, he says, begins exactly there.

“Unhuman Tour” (*Kusamakura*) (Sōseki; EN Kazutomo Takahashi, 1927; PG 73131). Sit through the unhuman world. Stop before the poet’s mission.

scenes.title: Climbing the mountain
scenes.reentry: Climbing the mountain, I was caught up into a train of thought.

breaths.text: Climbing the mountain, I was caught up into a train of thought.
Work with your brains, and you are liable to be harsh.
Punt in the stream of sentiment, and you may be carried away.
Heigh-ho, this is a disagreeable world to live in.
When the disagreeableness deepens, you wish to move to a world where life is less uneasy.
It is precisely when you awake to the truth, that move where you will, it will be hard to live, that poetry is born and art creates.
This human world of ours is the making neither of God nor of the Devil; but of common mortals; your neighbors on your right; your neighbors on your left, and your neighbors across the street.
Hate you may this world of common mortals, but where else can you go?
If anywhere else, it must be an unhuman world, but you will find an unhuman world a worse place to live in than this of humanity.
